content: The UCSD Medical Center is a prominent research hospital situated in the Hillcrest neighborhood of San Diego, California. Together with the UCSD Thornton Hospital in La Jolla, it serves as the primary teaching facility for the UC San Diego School of Medicine and the School of Pharmacy. The Hillcrest Center has 386 beds, while the Thornton Hospital has 119 beds, collectively forming the UCSD Medical Center. The medical center includes specialized facilities such as the Shiley Eye Center, the Moores Cancer Center, and the Trauma Center in Hillcrest. The Moores Cancer Center is the only comprehensive cancer center in the region, and the Trauma Center is one of only two Level 1 Trauma Centers in the area, the other being Scripps Mercy Hospital. The UCSD Medical Center is highly regarded for its significant contributions to healthcare in San Diego. In 2007, it was recognized by US News and World Report as one of the best hospitals in the nation in six specialty areas: 8th in respiratory disorders, 18th in rheumatology, 30th in kidney disease, 30th in gynecology, 39th in cancer, and 50th in ear, nose, and throat care. The Hillcrest Medical Center is the primary hospital for the UC San Diego School of Medicine and the region's only academic medical center. It provides both primary care and specialized services, including a full range of surgical procedures, genetic disease management, neurology, orthopedics, oncology, and sleep medicine. The recently renovated 386-bed hospital is also the main site for regional services such as the Comprehensive Organ Transplant Program, Bone Marrow Transplantation, the San Diego Regional Burn Center, the Infant Special Care Center (NICU), UCSD's Birth Center, San Diego County's only Level I Trauma Center, and the NIH-designated Clinical Research Center. The Thornton Hospital, officially named the John M. and Sally B. Thornton Hospital, opened in the summer of 1993 and has 119 beds. It is a medical-surgical facility offering a comprehensive range of services, including surgery, cardiology, endocrinology, neurology, orthopedics, oncology, reproductive medicine, and pulmonary medicine. The Rebecca and John Moores UCSD Cancer Center, established in 1979, is one of only 39 National Cancer Institute-designated Comprehensive Cancer Centers in the United States. These centers are recognized as leading institutions dedicated to scientific innovation and clinical excellence. The Moores Cancer Center is the only comprehensive cancer center in San Diego and Imperial counties to have earned this distinction. In 2007, the UCSD Medical Center was ranked 39th in the nation for cancer treatment by US News and World Report. The Shiley Eye Center at UCSD provides exceptional eye care for patients of all ages. Services range from basic eye exams to advanced diagnostic tests and sophisticated surgical procedures. The center is staffed by highly skilled physicians and offers comprehensive eye care at a single convenient location. Adjacent to the Shiley Eye Center is the Abraham Ratner Children's Eye Center, the only dedicated pediatric eye facility in the San Diego region, designed to address the unique vision needs of children. Services provided at the Shiley Eye Center include cataract surgery, cornea transplants, glaucoma diagnosis and treatment, low vision services, neuro-ophthalmology, optometry and contact lens services, pediatric ophthalmology, plastic surgery, refractive surgery, retina care, and trauma repair. On May 18, 2007, the UC Regents approved a plan to construct an additional inpatient tower in La Jolla, which will house 125 to 150 beds.
